newsitem.title: FINLAND: HELSINKI PARES LOSSES, SEEN FIRMER WITH EUROPE.
newsitem.headline: HELSINKI PARES LOSSES, SEEN FIRMER WITH EUROPE.

text.p: Shares trimmed losses across
the board in hesitant early afternoon Tuesday trade, recovering
from a weak start after New York's slide, and brokers said
stocks looked set to firm with European bourses.
"It looks like we're going to follow others upward," one
broker said, with the FOX futures index down 0.1 percent but
headed towards unchanged.
Nokia traded down 1.00 markka at 376.00 after
opening down sharply at 369.00 following a weak Monday session
on Wall Street. Nokia accounted for over a third of total
volume, which brokers said came mainly from overseas investors.
Brokers said a firmer bond market and a stronger dollar were
helping shares.
Valmet erased early losses to trade 0.40 markka
higher at 87.00 in solid 19 million markka dealings, and
Rautaruukki gained 1.00 markka to 52.10 in modest
trade.
Brokers said the market's hesitancy had more to do with an
absence of sellers than with a lack of buying interest.
--John Acher, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 235
